Messages.Author: dude_PL

Hey there,
I'm Marcin Szybkowski, I've been playing the game since 1996. I was the Prince of Warsaw between 2005 and 2010, where along with a friend of mine we built the Warsaw V:TES community, pretty much from the scratch. I was also the forum moderator for Polish V:TES community for several years. I've been responsible for coordinating national events and obtaining event support, both for the tournaments I organised and national events managed outside of my domain. I have successfully organised 3 National Qualifiers and 3 National Championship events in the last few years.

In Febuary 2010 I moved to Auckland, New Zealand and therefore passed the Prince title and responsibility to a friend of mine, who's been helping me for years. On a side note - it is quite ironic that when I moved out to another part of the globe, the European Championships actually hit my home town
Currently I'm looking at expanding the playgroup here in Auckland (which looks like a massive challenge, but we'll see how it goes) and hoping that I can make it to this year's Australian Championships.

I enjoy surprising people and I tend to play decks that make their minds explode - obviously they don't always work, but the fun factor is massive when they do

Ahh, the "Edge-Man" era. I remember it well; 1997-98.

There was a regional distributor in Texas who got stuck with a massive amount of Jyhad*, and for that reason and/or others they went bankrupt. The distributor's stock was bought at auction by a guy named Steve who ran an online store called "The Edge-Man". He fire-sold all of the Jyhad stock at $5 per box of boosters, $50 minimum purchase.

* It was somewhat well-known at the time jyhad came out that WotC was sending businesses Magic (in the era of The Dark and Legends) on a "percent allocation" against amount ordered, so some businesses were in the habit of gaming the allocation by ordering 3x to 5x more than they intended to sell, to try and grab a modestly larger share. The size of the Jyhad print run was big enough to fill 100% of what everyone ordered, and WotC was unwilling ot take any of it back, which is part of why the game got a bad rep with some distributors and retailers... This moment in VTES history was brought to you by the Old-Timey Cadre of Methuselah Cranks, of which atomweaver is a Founding Member.

Messages.Author: flarkit

Hi from South Africa

I've been playing VTES since roughly 1998, when a friend introduced me. I had fewer than 200 cards for a while, mostly a few donations and some boosters. I moved to a city with some stock which I started buying up until I was able to source lots more cards from the US (Ebay and Potomac Distribution FTW). These days I have probably 20,000 cards although I'm not a fervent collector. I prefer donating cards to new players in order to have people to play with and also prefer actually playing with the cards, than trying to have copies of amazing rares.

I find VTES much more enjoyable than the other CCG's I've tried, since it brings a strong social aspect to the game, along with the complex dynamics on 5-player tables and the huge variety of deck ideas.

Our playgroup in the adjoining cities of Johannesburg and Pretoria has see-sawed over the years, although there's a stable core group of about 6-8 people who've stuck around. These days there's some renewed interest again and we have a large group in far-away Cape Town which probably exceeds ours in both size and regularity of events.

It's incredibly saddening that WW's no longer supporting it, since we're enjoying good support here for a change. I only hope things will change again through the sustained support of the VTES community.

Personally, i want to punish blockers more. Id use isabel de leon (3cap g2 torrie with superior aus), maldavis mayne, and id run some target vitals with maybe one or two sniper rifles. Thats if i went weenie aus with it. More likely, id go with more celerity.

Id use sarah brando, 2 copies of volker, one victor tolliver and or parmeneides, and then:
Cut all or all but one aura reading, sidestrike, wwef, amd forced awakening. Id then add pursuits, one more concealed, run 5-6 44 magnums, more second trads, 1-2 parity shift, tension in the ranks, dragonbound, less tastes(6 probably max) possibly one or two resist earths grasp, possibly crocs tongue if you add bleed actions, some rushes, including one or more nose of hound, only one rack, and then:

You are still princes wall, with low cap princes, you fight and block some with supporters. I dont recall if powerbase monty is in that deck, but it should be. You sit and let table decelope early still, but then lategame and even midgame, you are a real risk to enemy actions. You could eagles sight and second trad and block most actions youd care about. Late game, weenie aus doesnt have the same bead removing efficiency as cel based combat, so id go with cel in combat here. I didn't realize that there *was* a thread for announcing yourself. I've been remiss.

My first name is Michael. I'm an attorney/philosopher living in Southern California (Orange County), where I don't get nearly enough time to play VTES.

I started playing the week the game came out, and haven't stopped. I'm not a heavy tournament player -- mostly because I'm busier than crap and I hate playing with time limits.

I hate master card decks and Pentex, think most of the Dark Sovereigns Location Master Cards should be errata'd to reduce their cost, believe strongly in the notion of house rules, prefer the Camarilla Edition format to all others both in terms of card layout and print quality, hold Villein to be a serious design mistake, hold the PTW rule in utter and total contempt, like playing Toolbox decks, can't stand it when people insist that the rules to this game are clear and unambiguous, and have spent more on sleeving my VTES decks than I did on Wine Futures last year.

I'm happy to be a part of the VEKN community, because this is the best game since Poker. I actually like it more than Poker, but I'm objectively realistic about the fact that Poker is just simply a better game.

Messages.Author: Antonin

Hello All!

I bought an Assamite Starter Deck many years ago at the Origins game convention in Columbus, Ohio, USA but I have never actually played V:TES. I'm a bit older than the gamers I used to meet at Origins, and really did not feel comfortable playing with people much younger than myself. For years I tried to find V:TES players closer to my own age, but no luck. It doesn't help that I'm an introvert with a very busy RL.

Anyway, while I don't know any other gamers in northeast Ohio, for years I have read and re-read the V:TES rules. I am also a big fan of the Dark Ages: Vampire novels from White Wolf.

At this point in my life (I'm close to retirement age and have other things on my mind) it's probably too late to think about playing V:TES face-to-face. But I would love to immerse myself in the game by reading about the gaming experiences of other people.

I wish V:TES had solitaire rules!

That is good to know!

A few years ago I went to a nearby comic book store looking for a group I could play Magic with. The store clerk was very friendly, but when I was looking nervously at the group of teenagers sitting at the gaming table, he said, "Hey! No problem! You're a kid at heart!"

I hated to tell him that no, I'm not a kid at heart. I'm just a middle-aged man with a wife and a full-time job who enjoys science fiction and fantasy novels. Nothing against all the happy teens at the comic book store and Origins playing card games, but the idea of joining them just felt strange.

Maybe someday I will play V:TES face to face with others, but for now I am happy to enjoy the game through the questions and stories of others here. I hope some of you will write about your gaming sessions!
